title: Minimax Supremum Risk for the Functional ATT Curve with Sparse Noisy Visits
banked_reason: Field-tier novelty cannot yet be supported without obtaining and comparing the underlying Bonvini–Kennedy–Keele manuscript or a theorem-level statement; the same N-thin-survey defect persisted after the root repair.
gap_reasons: The BonviniKennedyKeele2025 abstract is a close stated priority lead but has no inspectable theorem text, so field-tier novelty cannot yet be supported without obtaining and comparing the underlying manuscript or a theorem-level statement.

BergerHermannHolzmann2025 assumes independent sub-Gaussian errors at fixed synchronous design locations, not the stated two-period random-visit Gaussian kernel; relabel this as a new model condition or cite a source with the exact sampling law.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery reframed the random-arm presolve into a direct fixed-arm minimax program and specified a primitive correlated-sign hard family, an arm-split multiresolution estimator, and the proposed polynomial phase diagram. Two bounded repairs added the repository comparator, searched for primary BKK material, conceded the strongest plausible static overlap, and replaced the lower-bound witness by a pointwise class-membership certificate. The mathematics was not refuted, but field novelty remained unverified because only conference abstracts were available for the closest priority lead; no Stage D0 derivation or Lean proof was attempted.
tldr: For exactly n treated and n control subjects with m noisy random visits per period, determine the minimax expected supremum risk of the entire functional ATT curve. The proposed fixed-arm frontier has a mixed confounding and visit term of order \((n^2m)^{-2/15}\), up to logarithms, for \(1\le m\le n^{1/7}\). Resolving it would quantify how added measurements improve a causal curve estimate while leaving the number of independently observed covariates fixed.
